bodies.intuition: Batch size is how many examples the model looks at before each update. Larger batches give a cleaner estimate of the right direction and use hardware better, but past a point the extra examples stop buying accuracy and simply cost more. The useful range is set by that ceiling, not by memory.
bodies.engineer: Doubling the batch roughly halves the number of steps but only reduces gradient noise by √2, so throughput gains outrun quality gains and then stop. There is a critical batch size beyond which additional examples are close to wasted. Learning rate must scale with batch, or a larger batch simply trains slower per epoch.
bodies.math: Gradient variance falls as 1/|B|, so noise falls as 1/√|B| while cost rises linearly. Linear scaling η ∝ |B| holds until the critical batch size, past which the step count stops falling proportionally.

emphasis.intuition: set by that ceiling, not by memory

viz.caption: Share of the step's cost spent on the batch against everything else in the update. Drag the batch size to watch throughput and diminishing returns move together.
